papers.title: Trust in Machine Learning-Aided Docking: A Systematic Review of Good Practices for Chemically Reliable Predictions
papers.abstract: The massive growth of chemical libraries presents both an opportunity and a challenge in large-scale virtual screening. Machine learning (ML) algorithms have successfully accelerated this process with surrogate docking models that learn patterns between molecular representations and docking scores for ranking undocked molecules. Deep learning (DL), which represents the majority of ML-boosted docking approaches, has a sophisticated capability of finding nonlinear, complex relationships in voluminous data. However, DL algorithms operate as black boxes, face difficulties in generalization and raise concerns on whether correct predictions are, in fact, made for causal relationships between chemical structure and biological activity. Candidate molecules cannot be confidently tested if predictions are not understandable in human terms. The lack of understanding of relevant chemical properties impairs compound discovery, optimization and novelty, reinforcing the high-risk and high-cost scenario of drug design. To offer insights for expanding the recent breakthroughs achieved with the docking/ML integration, this review included 57 ML-aided docking papers from January 2020 to August 2026. We assessed how ML predictions are generated, refined and chemically interpreted to reliably reduce docking simulations and ideally increase experimental hit rates by data-driven and expert-driven decisions on compound selection. On this matter, the proper implementation of eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques is informative to elucidate if and how trustworthy are predicted hits from a chemical perspective, assuring a safer and more effective decision-making process for finding true hits. Nonetheless, only four (7.0%) out of 57 papers applied XAI techniques, mostly involving feature attribution methods, but not the state-of-the-art contrastive explanations method. Therefore, the implementation of XAI in ML-boosted docking is still scarce and needs formalization to avoid misinterpreting results. We review the various opportunities and limitations for integrating ML-aided docking with XAI techniques alongside complementary trust-enhancing strategies present in the included studies, such as sampling strategies, target diversity, ensemble and consensus docking, active learning, ensemble models, physicochemical and pharmacophore-based filtering, multiobjective optimization of molecular properties, confidence metrics of predefined acceptable errors, and expected model improvement along iterations. Given the broad applications of XAI across scientific domains and proof-of-concept studies in computational chemistry, we believe benchmarking and combining current and novel trust-enhancing strategies in ML-aided docking can go beyond finding initial hits. It supports both the statistical assessment including XAI in predictions and the mechanistic understanding of chemically relevant drug candidates for transparent and credible model and drug development.

papers.title: GA-VINO: A Geometry-Aware Variational Physics-Informed Neural Operator for Mindlin–Reissner Plates
papers.abstract: Plate and shell structures are widely used in engineering fields. Rapid response prediction for such structures under complex geometries, heterogeneous materials, and varying loads is important for engineering design, but conventional numerical methods usually require repeated modeling and solution when the physical configuration changes. To address this issue, this study proposes a geometry-aware variational physics-informed neural operator (GA-VINO) for Mindlin–Reissner plates. GA-VINO represents the plate geometry using boundary point clouds and incorporates a material encoder, a load encoder, and a scalar-parameter branch to handle spatially random material fields, spatially varying loads, and sample-level uniform parameters. Through multi-branch point cloud encoding and cross-attention, GA-VINO fuses geometric, material, loading, and query point information, and predicts the transverse deflection and rotations at arbitrary query locations. Unlike conventional data-driven neural operators, GA-VINO requires no labeled solution data during training. Instead, it minimizes a variational physics-informed loss constructed from the discretized total potential energy of the Mindlin–Reissner plate. Compared with grid-based neural operators, GA-VINO directly processes irregular point clouds and allows different physical fields to be discretized on different point sets, avoiding forced interpolation onto a common grid. Numerical results demonstrate that GA-VINO achieves accurate predictions across varying geometries, material properties, and loading conditions, with lower H 1 seminorm and energy-norm errors and more accurate predictions of bending moments and transverse shear forces than data-driven baselines. Furthermore, GA-VINO enables millisecond-level full-field inference and demonstrates useful generalization capability under moderate geometric distribution shifts, although its prediction accuracy decreases under stronger geometric extrapolation.

papers.title: Numerical simulation study of physical parameter compatibility principle for interlayer multi-material LPBF
papers.abstract: Multi-material laser powder bed fusion (multi-material LPBF) can meet the differentiated performance requirements of distinct regions in a single component, addressing the surging demand for integrated functional-structural forming. Among various multi-material LPBF approaches, interlayer multi-material LPBF can be readily implemented via single-material LPBF, making it the primary development direction of current multi-material LPBF. To establish the compatibility principle of physical parameter for interlayer multi-material LPBF, a numerical simulation investigation of interlayer multi-material LPBF based on the discrete element method framework Yade and the open-source finite volume method framework OpenFOAM was conducted, using 316L stainless steel and CuSn10 copper alloy as subjects. The theoretical models comprised the particle motion model based on the soft-sphere method, the mesoscopic molten pool dynamics model based on the multi-phase flow theory, and the laser heat source model based on the ray-tracing algorithm. The interlayer multi-material LPBF forming processes under different physical parameters (density, thermal conductivity, specific heat capacity, and viscosity) were predicted and the influences of each physical parameter on the transition zone were analyzed. It is found that the importance of each physical parameter to the transition zone follows the ranking: density>specific heat capacity>thermal conductivity>viscosity. Specifically, to achieve a thin transition zone with low intermixing effect, the upper material should exhibit smaller density, higher thermal conductivity, and larger specific heat capacity, with no requirement for viscosity. Conversely, to achieve a thick transition zone with strong intermixing effect, the upper material should have a higher density, lower thermal conductivity, and smaller specific heat capacity, while viscosity remains non-constraining. This study is expected to provide scientific guidance for the development of interlayer multi-material LPBF forming specifications. The open-source code of this study is available at https://github.com/caoliu0706/5-Multi-material-LPBF .

papers.title: Functional Outcomes in Smokers Following Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty: A Narrative Review
papers.abstract: Smoking is associated with perioperative complications after total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA), and in 2021, most English commissioners had smoking-related access policies for these operations. Its association with functional recovery is less certain. This narrative review, guided by the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA), synthesizes evidence on smoking status and function after primary THA and TKA. PubMed was searched from inception to November 2, 2026, and 26 primary studies reporting function, baseline status, or related outcomes by smoking status were appraised. All functional evidence identified was observational. In the largest baseline-adjusted analysis (10,009 patients across both joints, representing 8.6% of the source cohort), smokers improved substantially. However, their six-month Oxford Hip and Knee Scores were 2.5 and 3.2 points lower than those of nonsmokers. The upper limits of the 95% confidence intervals (3.5 and 4.5 points) fell below the between-group minimal important difference of approximately 5 points, although the TKA limit exceeded the original authors' 4-point threshold. Smaller cohorts generally reported lower scores or smaller gains, whereas responder analyses were mixed, and two TKA recovery-modeling studies with few current smokers were inconclusive. Registry analyses linked smoking with slower or less sustained recovery after THA, and current smokers reported more pain after TKA. Smokers had worse preoperative scores, and confounding was rarely fully addressed. No trial identified has measured functional outcomes after cessation, and observational cessation data are limited and affected by early relapse. Smokers gain substantial function but achieve modestly lower average scores than nonsmokers. The gap appears to be below the usual threshold for a clinically important group difference, but this conclusion rests largely on one dataset with incomplete outcome data, and its causal basis remains uncertain. The evidence supports cessation support for perioperative safety but does not show that quitting improves function or justify withholding surgery.

papers.title: Surrogate-assisted design optimisation method for steel-concrete joints in large-span hybrid girder bridges using machine learning
papers.abstract: Steel-concrete joints play a critical role in force transfer in large-span hybrid girder bridges, where multiple structural parameters interact in a highly nonlinear manner. Conventional parametric analysis is often insufficient for efficient performance evaluation and design optimisation. In this article, an application-oriented surrogate-assisted design optimisation framework was established for steel-concrete joints by integrating finite element (FE) analysis, machine learning (ML) and multi-objective decision-making. A database was established based on detailed FE models covering various design parameter combinations of common hybrid girder bridges. Six ML algorithms were trained and evaluated, and the best-performing models were selected as surrogate models for predicting force transfer performance indicators. The results indicate that LightGBM and XGBoost achieve high predictive accuracy for the uniformity indices of the back and front cells, respectively. Based on the surrogate models, Pareto-based multi-objective optimisation was conducted considering force transfer uniformity and equivalent economic performance related to material consumption, construction complexity and carbon-related effects. Finally, a preferred design parameter combination can be selected by the comprehensive indicator with different weight coefficients. The proposed framework provides a systematic data-driven procedure for evaluating, interpreting, and selecting design parameter combinations of steel-concrete joints, while reducing the computational cost of repeated FE analyses.

papers.title: Implante de carga imediata seguido de enxerto autógeno: relato de caso clínico
papers.abstract: Immediate loading dental implants associated with autogenous bone grafts have stood out as an efficient alternative for oral rehabilitation, providing satisfactory functional and aesthetic results in a shorter treatment time. This study aims to report a clinical case of immediate loading implant followed by autogenous grafting, highlighting its importance in bone preservation, implant stability, and aesthetic recovery of the patient. This is a descriptive study based on a clinical case report and literature review, addressing the main indications, advantages, and limitations of the technique. The association of autogenous grafting with immediate loading implants favors osseointegration, maintenance of gingival tissues, and preservation of alveolar bone volume, in addition to providing greater comfort and self-esteem to the patient. The results demonstrate that the technique presents high clinical predictability when properly planned and performed. It is concluded that immediate loading implants associated with autogenous grafts constitute a safe and effective alternative for oral rehabilitation, promoting functional, aesthetic, and psychological benefits.

papers.title: Effect of posterior longitudinal ligament resection on biomechanical characteristics in cervical disc arthroplasty: a finite element analysis
papers.abstract: The posterior longitudinal ligament (PLL) plays a critical role in maintaining the biomechanical integrity. However, the biomechanical impact of PLL resection on the cervical spine remains a subject of debate. This study aimed to use finite element analysis (FEA) to determine the effects of PLL resection versus preservation on the biomechanics after cervical disc arthroplasty (CDA). A validated finite element model of the cervical spine (C3-C7) was developed based on computed tomography data from a patient with mild degenerative changes at C5-C6. At this level, a CDA model was constructed and implanted with three cervical disc prostheses (Bryan, Mobi-C, and Prodisc-C). For each prosthesis, both PLL-preserved and PLL-resected surgical models were established. Two distinct mechanical loading protocols were applied, namely identical axial preload with 1.0 Nm moment and displacement loading. The analyzed parameters encompassed range of motion (ROM), intervertebral disc stress (IDS), facet joint stress (FJS), bone-implant interface stress (BIS), prosthesis stress (PS). Compared with the preoperative condition, ROM increased at the operative segment (C5-C6) following all three disc replacements, indicating increased segmental ROM. Regarding the comparison between PLL resection and preservation, the majority of biomechanical parameters remained largely unchanged. However, a few notable exceptions were observed. Among them, the Bryan artificial disc exhibited the most pronounced change, with a 10.08% reduction in BIS during extension following PLL resection. The Prodisc-C demonstrated the greatest variation at the operative segment (C5-C6), where PS increased by 6.77% during extension while BIS decreased by approximately 3.5% during lateral bending, while changes during flexion (− 0.41%) and rotation (− 0.16%) were negligible. Aside from these isolated instances, all other parameter changes between PLL resection and preservation were minimal, generally remaining below 1%. Under the simulated quasi-static loading conditions, resection of the PLL during CDA did not meaningfully alter postoperative biomechanical outcomes. ROM at the operative segment was consistently increased regardless of the prosthesis type or PLL management strategy, and the few parameter variations observed between resection and preservation were minor under the simulated conditions. These findings suggest that biomechanical considerations alone need not drive the decision to resect the PLL; rather, the decision should be individualized based on the need for adequate decompression and patient-specific pathology.

papers.title: Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty in Adults With Osteogenesis Imperfecta: A Systematic Review of Surgical Techniques, Complications, and Outcomes
papers.abstract: Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) is a heritable disorder of bone fragility that can lead to progressive deformity, altered joint mechanics, and early degenerative disease. Total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA) can improve pain and function in adults with OI, but small bone dimensions, poor bone quality, deformity, ligamentous laxity, prior fracture surgery, and abnormal anatomy make reconstruction difficult. This systematic review summarizes surgical techniques, complications, revisions, and functional outcomes reported after lower-extremity arthroplasty in adults with OI. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched without publication-date restrictions; database searches were conducted between September 1 and October 20, 2026. Adults aged 18 years or older undergoing primary or revision THA or TKA were eligible when OI-specific clinical data were extractable. Case reports, case series, and observational studies were included because of the limited literature. Overlapping cohorts were reconciled at the patient and joint level. Twenty primary studies published from 1993 to 2023 contributed 34 adults and 43 qualifying joints: 29 hips (67.4%) and 14 knees (32.6%). Nineteen patients (55.9%) were female, and the median age at the earliest qualifying arthroplasty was 48.5 years (range, 24-69 years). Single-patient reports contributed 14 (41.2%) of 34 adults and 15 (34.9%) of 43 joints. Hip reconstruction included cemented, cementless, hybrid, and revision-specific constructs. Knee reconstruction was usually cemented when fixation was reported and often required stems, increased constraint, or corrective osteotomy. At least eight intraoperative fracture events were reported across distinct operative contexts: two during primary THA, four during revision THA, and two during TKA performed with corrective osteotomy; these events were not pooled into a single procedure-level rate. Long-term hip series showed improved function but a substantial revision burden. Knee reports generally described improved pain and function, with reoperations more often related to stiffness or osteotomy healing than prosthetic loosening. THA and TKA are feasible in selected adults with OI, but the published experience remains dominated by small, noncomparative studies and is limited by retrospective reporting, publication bias, and heterogeneous operative contexts.

papers.title: Intent Representation and Human Distraction Modulate the Effects of Legible Robot Motion in Hallway Navigation
papers.abstract: Legibility in human-robot interaction (HRI) is often described as the property of robot motion that enables an observer to confidently and quickly infer the robot’s intent. Mature frameworks exist for generating legible motion in front of static observers, typically by making the robot’s destination apparent as early as possible. Social robot navigation in public spaces, however, presents a different challenge: pedestrians are themselves in motion, often with divided attention, and must coordinate with the robot in real time. In such encounters, where the robot is ultimately headed may matter less to a pedestrian than how it intends to pass them. This raises two questions: which aspect of intent should legible motion convey, and does legibility remain beneficial when pedestrians are not fully attentive to the robot? We address these questions in the ubiquitous and demanding scenario of hallway navigation, through two controlled user studies comparing multiple legibility formulations implemented within a shared model predictive control framework. Study 1 ( N = 45) compares destination-based and passing-side intent representations, showing that the latter, particularly when adaptively updated, allows for smoother human motion and is perceived as more competent and less mentally and physically demanding than the former. Study 2 ( N = 45) examines the effect of pedestrian attention, demonstrating that legible motion supports smooth human motion even under distraction, although this benefit is not consistently reflected in subjective ratings. Together, these findings suggest that effective legible motion in social robot navigation benefits from interaction-level intent representations that support coordination, with some effects persisting even when human attention is divided. Code is available at https://github.com/fluentrobotics/Legible_MPPI and footage from our experiments at https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P5O5BwfcUCo .

papers.title: Adaptive phase-shift control of LCC resonant converters with transformer-insulation micro-arcing risk awareness
papers.abstract: High-voltage LCC resonant converters are widely used in applications such as X-ray devices, but they face severe reliability challenges. Conventional phase-shift control often exacerbates internal voltage fluctuations across the high-voltage transformer windings. This can induce internal transformer-insulation micro-arcing and accelerate dielectric failure. To address this issue, this paper proposes an adaptive phase-shift control method with transformer-insulation micro-arcing risk awareness. First, this study analyzes the disturbance caused by the micro-arcing incubation process on the resonant tank. This analysis reveals the physical coupling mechanism between phase-shift angle variations and local electric field distortion. Subsequently, key electrical features are selected to construct a physics-informed neural network (PINN). These features include the complementary winding voltage difference, the third harmonic of the resonant current, and the current change rate. The model embeds circuit law residuals and physical boundaries. This overcomes the generalization limits of data-driven methods in small-sample high-voltage scenarios. Consequently, it achieves real-time, accurate, and highly interpretable quantification of micro-arcing risk. Finally, an adaptive phase-shift control law is designed. It utilizes the risk probability and its rate of change as feedforward compensation signals. This strategy dynamically and smoothly adjusts the phase-shift angle to optimize the electric field distribution. Therefore, it proactively suppresses the occurrence of micro-arcing. Compared to conventional phase-shift control, this method significantly narrows the voltage peak distribution at critical insulation points. It effectively reduces the probability of micro-arcing events whilst maintaining a stable output voltage.

papers.title: Microstructural regulation enables strength-ductility synergy and superior high-temperature performance in additively manufactured ECY768 cobalt-based superalloy
papers.abstract: ECY768 is a promising cobalt-based superalloy for hot-section components in aerospace and energy applications, yet its fabrication process by laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) remains insufficiently explored. This study investigates the microstructure and tensile behavior of LPBF ECY768 alloy in the as-built (AB), solution treated (ST), direct aging treated (AT), and solution aging treated (SAT) conditions. Results indicate that the highly dense AB alloy shows a mixed columnar-equiaxed grain structure containing cellular dendritic sub-grain. MC-type carbides and M 23 C 6 -type carbides are distributed along cellular boundaries. Although the AB alloy has a certain of anisotropy in tensile properties, it achieves substantially higher room temperature strength and ductility than cast cobalt-based superalloy, owing to the synergistic strengthening of the cellular dislocation networks and carbides. ST induces recovery and recrystallization, causing grain equiaxialization and clear reductions in carbide content and dislocation density. Consequently, strength decreases but elongation increases by more than 20%. AT preserves the original grain morphology but coarsens carbides and raises their fraction, thereby enhancing strength at the expense of ductility. SAT produces recrystallized grains with moderate carbide fraction and dislocation density, realizing a favorable strength-ductility balance with anisotropy below 5%. High-temperature tensile testing at 540°C, 750°C, and 900°C reveals a continuous reduction in strength, whereas elongation exhibits an initial increase followed by a decrease for both AB and SAT conditions. Correspondingly, the fracture modes evolve from transgranular to mixed transgranular-intergranular and to predominantly intergranular. Overall, the LPBF ECY768 alloy demonstrates high strength and appreciable ductility across a wide temperature range, highlighting its engineering potential.

papers.title: Electronic Structure of Co-Phthalocyanine Metal–Organic Framework
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) composed of metal phthalocyanines (MPc; MPc-MOF) are predicted to possess electronic structures similar to those of Dirac materials, such as the Lieb lattice and the fes lattice. Therefore, in this study, we first investigated the energy band structure of CoPc-MOF using density functional theory (DFT). According to previous theoretical studies, if the lattice structure of CoPc-MOF is regarded as a Lieb lattice, its π-band is predicted to exhibit stronger Dirac-band-like characteristics compared to other MPc-MOFs containing metals. The electron density obtained from the energy band calculations indicated that the contribution of the central metal to the π-band of CoPc-MOF is small; therefore, the lattice structure can be assumed to be more similar to the fes lattice than to the Lieb lattice. Next, we evaluated the crystal structure of the synthesized CoPc-MOF using X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The TEM images revealed that the synthesized CoPc-MOF powder consists of flake-like microcrystals, in which crystal growth along the molecular layer stacking direction is minimal. Furthermore, the absorption spectra in the visible and near-infrared (Vis–NIR) regions indicate that CoPc-MOF is a narrow-gap semiconductor with an optical gap of approximately 0.36 eV. On the other hand, DFT calculations indicate that the CoPc-MOF crystal is metallic due to the formation of a π-band in the interlayer direction (along the c-axis), which is inconsistent with the experimental results. This suggests that the synthesized CoPc-MOF may not be sufficiently stacked in the interlayer direction. This finding is consistent with the TEM images, which show that CoPc-MOF consists of flake-like microcrystalline structures. Energy band calculations were performed on a single monolayer of CoPc-MOF; however, even a single monolayer of CoPc-MOF behaves as a metal when electronic correlations are not explicitly considered, which contradicts the Vis–NIR and UPS experimental results. The single molecular layer of CoPc-MOF exhibited a metallic ground state because the π-d bands near the Fermi level formed the Fermi surface. In conclusion, the DFT+U energy-band calculations for the CoPc-MOF monolayer reproduced a semiconducting ground state and best explained the UPS spectra. These results indicate that the electronic correlation effects are significant in the 2D π-d bands near the Fermi level of a single molecular layer of CoPc-MOF.

papers.title: Characterizing the Influence of Alloy Compositional Variation on the Wetting Behavior and Surface Tension of Liquid Al 7xxx Alloys
papers.abstract: This study systematically investigates the wettability and surface tension of seven calculation of phase diagrams (CALPHAD)-designed Al 7xxx alloys developed for laser powder bed fusion (LPBF). The alloys comprised the following: Al7075, Al7075–1V, Al7075–1V–1Mg, Al7075–1V–2Mg, Al7075–1V–1Ti, Al7075–1V–1Ti–1Mg, and Al7075–1V–1Ti–2Mg for Alloys 1 to 7, respectively (additions in wt pct). Sessile drop experiments were conducted on alumina substrates under argon from 923 K to 1523 K. Surface tension was also evaluated using a CALPHAD-coupled modified Guggenheim formulation over 932 K to 1673 K and a CALPHAD-coupled multicomponent Butler model over 932 K to 1523 K. The experimental results revealed that contact angles decreased with temperature for all alloys, with Alloy 1 remaining nonwetting up to 1273 K before wetting improved markedly. The experimental surface tension ranged from 718.87 to 1079.80 mN m −1 , whereas the CALPHAD predictions (modified Guggenheim formulation) ranged from 746.07 to 843.71 mN m −1 . Alloy 1 exhibited an experimental nonmonotonic response, increasing from 766.74 mN m −1 at 923 K to 884.85 mN m −1 at 1273 K before decreasing to 811.08 mN m −1 at 1523 K. Fitted experimental temperature coefficients were positive for Alloys 4 and 7 and negative for Alloys 2, 3, 5, and 6. In contrast, both thermodynamic approaches predicted negative temperature coefficients for all seven alloys. Butler calculations showed strong Mg surface enrichment and decreasing equilibrium surface tension with increasing Mg content, whereas V and Ti were strongly surface depleted. Post-test energy-dispersive spectroscopy revealed oxygen-rich surface regions and substantial Mg and Zn compositional changes. Overall, equilibrium alloy composition and surface segregation explain part of the surface tension response, whereas oxygen-related surface modification and possible elemental volatilization may contribute to the remaining experimental behavior. These results support the heat transfer–fluid flow modeling of the melt pool dynamics of LPBF-processed aluminum alloys.

papers.title: Systematic evaluation of machine learning and explainable AI for NOx emission prediction in gas turbine systems
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions is essential for improving environmental sustainability, regulatory compliance, and operational efficiency in gas turbine systems. However, the complex nonlinear interactions among environmental and operational variables make reliable emission forecasting challenging using conventional modeling approaches. This study presents a comprehensive machine learning and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) framework for NOx emission prediction using the Gas Turbine CO and NOx Emission dataset from the UCI Machine Learning Repository. Ten regression algorithms, including linear, tree-based, ensemble, and gradient-boosting models, were systematically evaluated and optimized using Grid Search, Random Search, and Bayesian Optimization. Model performance was assessed using multiple regression metrics, including R², MAE, MSE, RMSE, MAPE, EVS, and MedAE. Among all evaluated approaches, Bayesian-optimized LightGBM achieved the best predictive performance with an R² score of 0.8928 and an RMSE of 3.7694. To enhance model transparency, multiple complementary XAI techniques, including SHAP, Permutation Feature Importance, Partial Dependence Plots, Individual Conditional Expectation, LIME, surrogate modeling, and residual analysis, were employed. The explainability results consistently identified ambient temperature, turbine inlet temperature, gas turbine exhaust pressure, and turbine after temperature as the dominant factors influencing NOx emissions. The proposed framework demonstrates that high predictive accuracy and interpretability can be achieved simultaneously, providing a promising and transparent approach for NOx emission prediction in gas turbine systems.

papers.title: Large language model surrogates for Bayesian optimization of antibody sequences
papers.abstract: Enhancing therapeutic antibody properties typically requires iterative sequence engineering and experimental validation, such as binding assays, making antibody optimization time-consuming and resource intensive. To address these challenges, we introduce AbL2BO, a Bayesian optimization (BO) framework integrating a large language model (LLM) with Bayesian fine-tuning. AbL2BO leverages prior knowledge embedded in an antibody-specific LLM and efficiently updates model parameters using Bayesian Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) with approximate inference, including the Laplace approximation or MC dropout. The fine-tuned LLM serves as a surrogate model within the BO framework. Our results show that AbL2BO achieves superior sample efficiency compared to conventional BO methods that rely on Gaussian process regression to model black-box functions. Across experimental and simulated benchmark datasets, AbL2BO consistently demonstrated competitive or superior optimization performance with better-calibrated uncertainty estimates than kernel-based BO approaches. Integrating LLMs into BO offers three key advantages: (1) warm-starting the optimization with pretrained knowledge; (2) easy adaptation to new domains; and (3) bypassing the complexities of kernel design choices, kernel computation, and sequence alignment to handle sequences of varying length. Overall, AbL2BO improves both optimization efficiency and uncertainty estimation, particularly for complex antibody sequence landscapes, with the potential to reduce time and resource requirements in therapeutic antibody development.

papers.title: How to Teach Data Literacy Through Real-World Examples
papers.abstract: This presentation was developed for the Digital Research Academy's Train-the-Trainer Programme #9 (Online) and delivered on 20 November 2026. The session explores how familiar, real-world situations can be used to teach data literacy without relying on technical explanations or statistical formulas. Through everyday examples, participants practise questioning data claims, identifying misleading conclusions, and reflecting on how these activities can be adapted to different learning contexts. The workshop combines individual reflection, group discussions, and hands-on exercises. Participants also design their own short teaching activities, focusing on active learning, meaningful learner engagement, and ways to check understanding. The session draws on principles of adult learning, evidence-based teaching, and the ICAP framework. Learning objectives: Select relatable real-world examples appropriate for different audiences. Design activities that encourage learners to question, interpret, and explain data. Develop simple ways to assess whether learners can apply what they have learned. The numerical scenarios used in the exercises are fictional and were developed for educational purposes.

papers.title: Hydroxamate Reticular Chemistry beyond Metals: Single-Crystalline Two- and Three-Dimensional Boron–Hydroxamate Covalent Organic Frameworks
papers.abstract: Hydroxamate chelation has already enabled robust metal–organic frameworks. Here, to move the corresponding reticular chemistry beyond metal nodes, hydroxamate chelation has been integrated within heteroleptic tetracoordinate B(O,O)(N)(C) centers to construct four single-crystalline boron–hydroxamate covalent organic frameworks, namely SUM-306–SUM-309. Bayesian optimization enabled the growth of diffraction-quality SUM-306 single crystals, while linker isomerism and functionalization yielded a series spanning two-dimensional hcb and three-dimensional pcu-h frameworks. Structural comparison reveals extended anti-B–phenylene–B arrangements in SUM-306 and SUM-307 and folded syn arrangements in SUM-308 and SUM-309, associated with their respective two- and three-dimensional propagation. Solid-state NMR spectroscopy, B K-edge XANES, and electronic-structure calculations support tetracoordinate boron formation and differentiated yet substantial bonding throughout the B(O,O)(N)(C) environment. As a representative of the series, SUM-308 retains accessible microporosity, exhibits a BET surface area of 1279.9 m2 g–1, and preferentially adsorbs and dynamically separates CO2 from N2. These results extend hydroxamate reticular chemistry beyond metals and establish a mixed-linkage strategy combining chelation, donor–acceptor coordination, and covalent anchoring for single-crystalline boron-based framework construction.

papers.title: Fruit3DGS: Fruit-agnostic counting and localization leveraging semantic-guided 3D Gaussian Splatting and contrastive learning
papers.abstract: Fruit counting and localization are essential for yield estimation, crop monitoring, and robotic harvesting. We introduce Fruit3DGS, a fruit-agnostic framework that combines semantic-guided 3D Gaussian Splatting with contrastive instance learning to reconstruct, count, and localize fruits from unordered multi-view RGB images. Existing semantic radiance-field approaches often rely on fruit-specific clustering parameters, predefined size priors, or geometric templates, which limits their transfer across different fruit categories and acquisition conditions. To reduce this dependency, Fruit3DGS augments each Gaussian primitive with a semantic coefficient and a contrastive instance embedding. Prompt-driven binary and instance masks predicted by vision foundation models provide the supervision required to learn foreground semantics and view-consistent fruit identities directly in the 3D representation. Foreground Gaussians are subsequently grouped through a seeded microcluster-merge procedure operating on an embedding-augmented k -nearest-neighbor graph, with its hyperparameters selected automatically through Bayesian optimization. The resulting clusters provide individual fruit instances, predicted counts, and oriented bounding boxes for metric 3D localization without requiring fruit-size templates. We evaluate Fruit3DGS on 14 counting datasets and eight scenes with ground-truth 3D fruit positions. The method remains competitive on established apple-counting benchmarks and transfers more reliably than the original FruitNeRF pipeline to the evaluated non-apple and mixed-fruit scenes. Across the eight localization scenes, Fruit3DGS achieves the lowest mean localization error on seven scenes and an average scene-level mean error of 4.74 cm, compared with 30.29 cm for original FruitNeRF, 56.13 cm for FruitNeRF with an HDBSCAN backend, and 8.49 cm for FruitNeRF++ features clustered with HDBSCAN. This corresponds to a 44.2% reduction in average localization error relative to the strongest competing baseline, FruitNeRF++–HDBSCAN. The results demonstrate that combining semantic-guided Gaussian splatting with contrastive embedding learning enables accurate, fruit-agnostic 3D reconstruction and reliable instance-level perception, while retaining the real-time rendering capability of the optimized 3DGS representation for agricultural robotics and precision-farming applications.

papers.title: A prediction–optimization–decision framework for logistics network design under demand and disruption uncertainty
papers.abstract: Aiming at the problem of the separation of logistics network design prediction and optimization under the double uncertainty of dynamic demand and disruption risk, this paper proposes a prediction-optimization-decision integration framework with deep integration of machine learning and system optimization. The framework adopts a three-layer architecture: the prediction layer constructs a hybrid model combining spatial-temporal graph neural network and multi-head attention mechanism and uses deep ensembles and quantile regression to quantify epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty. The risk layer identifies disruption risks through attention-based multi-label classification and deep support vector data description and generates a representative risk scenario set combining multi-layer network propagation model and importance sampling. The optimization layer establishes a multi-period mixed integer programming model and introduces resilience service level constraints and conditional value-at-risk measurement to realize the synergy between cost and resilience. In order to solve large-scale problems, a learning-enhanced large-scale neighborhood search algorithm is designed, and reinforcement learning agents are embedded in the operator selection process. The experimental results show that the MAE of the proposed prediction model is reduced by 8.2% to 15.6% compared with Transformer in each step. The average F1 of risk classification reached 0.847, 6.2% higher than that of XGBoost. The total cost of the optimization algorithm is 13.4% lower than that of stochastic programming on large-scale instances, and the optimality gap reaches 0.8% within 600 s. The total cost of the framework in 12 months decreased by 16.9%, the service level improved by 5.6% points, and the interruption recovery time shortened by 62%.

papers.title: Additive Manufacturing and Mechanical Characterisation of COC/TiO₂/CNT Composite Filaments for 3D-Printed Static Mixers
papers.abstract: Cyclic olefin copolymer (COC)-based composite filaments containing TiO₂ and carbon nanotubes (CNTs) were developed for fused filament fabrication (FFF) of functional static mixer structures. The influence of filler composition (1.5–3 wt% TiO₂ and 0–0.5 wt% CNTs) on filament processability, mechanical performance, and printability was systematically evaluated. Composite filaments were produced via twin-screw melt compounding and extruded to a diameter of 1.75 mm, followed by FFF of tensile specimens and static mixers. Mechanical properties of the printed specimens were determined according to ISO 527-2:2025. Additionally, tensile work to fracture was obtained from the tensile testing software as a supplementary metric representing the mechanical work recorded up to specimen fracture. TiO₂ addition had minimal impact on tensile strength and printability, whereas CNT incorporation progressively reduced tensile strength (by up to 68 % relative to the corresponding TiO₂-only formulation), elongation, and tensile work to fracture. All formulations exhibited stable extrusion, uniform filament formation, and defect-free printing without warping or clogging. Young’s modulus ranged from 450 to 870 MPa. The study demonstrates that COC/TiO₂/CNT hybrid systems can be successfully processed under the selected conditions for the FFF fabrication of geometrically complex flow components, enabling direct fabrication of static mixers for process intensification applications.

papers.title: A predictive and reinforcement learning-driven framework for adaptive cybersecurity training and behavioral risk mitigation
papers.abstract: Phishing attacks continue to become more sophisticated and employee behavior is still a major part of the organization’s cyber security strategy. This study introduces a behavior-aware framework to predict the phishing susceptibility through supervised learning, clustering (unsupervised learning techniques), and reinforcement learning and to provide the customized cybersecurity training. The framework was created based on an augmented dataset, which takes into account phishing simulation data along with Human Resource (HR) data, such as demographic, behavioral, and organizational attributes. The accuracy, F1 Score, ROC-AUC, and confusion matrix were used to assess the accuracy of the five ensemble learning algorithms (Random Forest (RF), XGBoost (XGB), Extra Trees (ET), LightGBM (LGBM) and soft Voting Ensemble). Among the baseline classifiers, ET outperforms as compared to other by achieving accuracy (80%), and F1-score (79%) with ROC-AUC (0.88) which was good for discriminative power over decision thresholds. To identify various behavioral personas of employee ‘s behaviour, K-Means clustering algorithm was applied. The optimal clustering solution was determined using silhouette analysis, which was followed by one-way ANOVA that revealed a significant difference in the groups’ phishing risk and their engagement and participation in training. These behavioral profiles create interpretable basis to create specific cybersecurity interventions. The framework is designed to build on these insights and uses Q-learning to adapt training approaches based on the user’s behavior response instead of using fixed training programs based on awareness. To the best of our knowledge, this is among the first framework to integrate phishing susceptibility prediction, behavioral segmentation, and adaptive based reinforcement training within unified human-centered cybersecurity architecture.

papers.title: How Assessment and Feedback Vary Across Areas of Knowledge: University Students’ Perspectives
papers.abstract: Feedback is a fundamental pillar of active learning and formative assessment in Higher Education, yet its implementation is often shaped by the pedagogical traditions across different areas of knowledge. This study analyses university students’ perceptions of assessment and feedback practices, focusing on how areas of knowledge influence assessment tools use, sources, delivery modes, formats, and timing of feedback. Conducted with a cross-sectional quantitative design, the study draws on a sample of 1,841 students from universities in Catalonia and Andorra. Principal component analysis identified seven factors structuring assessment tools and feedback practices. Results reveal considerable variation in the use of assessment tools across areas of knowledge; whereas feedback practices remain relatively similar. Findings indicate a low frequency of active assessment models and a persistence of traditional approaches to feedback practices, characterized by unidirectional teacher feedback mostly provided at the end of the process. Self-assessment and peer feedback remain limited. These findings suggest that “disciplinary cultures” primarily shape the use of assessment tools, whereas feedback practices vary less across fields. Practical implications point out the need to promote more dialogic, reflective, and self-regulated pedagogical designs to foster deep and sustainable learning, while remaining consistent with the specificities of each area of knowledge.

papers.title: Distributed Interactive Conformal Prediction for Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems increasingly rely on learning-enabled components and distributed algorithms for perception, estimation, and control, introducing uncertainty that makes it challenging to satisfy mission requirements. Conformal prediction quantifies uncertainty with distribution-free guarantees, but existing methods do not address the challenging combination of dependence among robots, distributed calibration, and the distribution shift induced when calibrated uncertainty bounds modify the closed-loop system. We introduce Multi-Agent Interactive Conformal Prediction (MA-ICP), a distributed framework for computing robustness margins in heterogeneous systems to satisfy mission requirements with high probability. MA-ICP aggregates robot-level nonconformity scores, which measure errors in modeled or estimated quantities, into one mission-level score per robot class, allowing dependence among robots within each mission. Mission-level scores and quantiles are computed using neighbor-to-neighbor communication in a finite number of communication rounds. Updating the robustness margins changes robot trajectories and distributed algorithm outputs, so we use class-dependent score sensitivities to upper bound the shift in mission-level scores. We then establish calibration-conditional coverage guarantees per robot class for the updated margins. We demonstrate MA-ICP on cooperative payload control, formation control with obstacle avoidance, and distributed target tracking missions.

papers.abstract: Marine robots face partial observability, non-stationary dynamics, and sparse communication, motivating WMs that learn compact predictive states for planning. This review develops a functional taxonomy of WMs for ocean engineering, focusing on Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) and AdaJEPA's test-time adaptation within model predictive control, mapping them to navigation, adaptive sampling, digital twins, and biodiversity monitoring, and separating demonstrated evidence from prospective applications. The synthesis identifies key Gaps: benchmarks, uncertainty calibration, safe adaptation and proposes a research agenda for physics-informed, deployment-adaptive marine WMs validated through simulation and field missions.

papers.title: Learning Land-Surface Hydrology World Model from Satellite Observations
papers.abstract: A world model should tell us not only what will happen, but what would happen under a different action. Learned Earth models now forecast remarkably well, yet forecast skill says little about what their state means or how it responds to a changed driver. We build LandWM, a world model of land-surface water in which rain is the action, learned from seven years of SMAP and CYGNSS observations: physical observation operators tie its latent state to soil water, and a mass-conserving balance governs how that state responds to rain. Over the U.S. Southern Great Plains, the model, never shown a soil-moisture value, tracks 28 in-situ probes as well as the operational SMAP Level-4 product, even from CYGNSS alone, and a storm added to the forcing of a station's cell wets its soil as natural storms wet the probes. Replace either piece and the forecasts stay, but the meaning goes: with neural operators, only a probe fitted to the stations finds the soil water; with a generic recurrent transition, rain on a single cell barely moves it. Yet when the same rain covers the whole region the two transitions swap roles, and the conserving one responds too weakly. Grounding makes a world model readable; its response to actions must be tested under more than one kind of intervention.

papers.title: An Efficient Long-Time Stable Second-Order Ensemble Method for the Parameterized Navier--Stokes Equations
papers.abstract: Ensemble simulations for uncertainty quantification, ensemble forecasting, and long-time statistics require stability over arbitrarily long horizons without time-step restrictions. We develop a second-order ensemble method for parameterized incompressible Navier--Stokes equations that uses a common, time-independent Brinkman (shifted Stokes) operator for all members. The scheme combines BDF2, a mean-reverting scalar auxiliary variable (mr-SAV) treatment of convection, and viscosity splitting with a shared viscosity $\barν$ treated implicitly and memberwise deviations explicitly. For constant viscosities satisfying $0<ν_j<4\barν/3$, we establish unconditional, uniform-in-time dissipativity under uniformly bounded forcing, including an absorbing bound independent of initial data and time-step size. We show that the upper viscosity threshold is sharp for fixed $\barν$. For spatially varying random viscosities, unconditional long-time stability holds under a signed pointwise condition that confines $ν_j$ to $(\barν/3,4\barν/3)$ uniformly away from the endpoints; for proportional spatial profiles, it holds over the full range $0<ν_j<4\barν/3$. Under the full-range constant-viscosity condition and sufficient regularity in two dimensions, we prove second-order temporal error bounds for velocity, the auxiliary variable, and the discrete time primitive of the pressure error. Numerical tests corroborate long-time stability at large time steps and the sharpness of the viscosity threshold, demonstrate accurate individual solutions and ensemble statistics, and show that mean reversion prevents long-time drift. Reusing the shared operator reduces computing time by about half relative to member-by-member solves.

papers.abstract: Executable code can preserve a world's structural layout, yet video renderers frequently alter the appearance of previously visited places once they leave the camera view. We present Paintress, a code-conditioned world model that couples an executable geometric proxy with an independently parameterized 3D Gaussian appearance memory in a shared metric coordinate frame. While the proxy enforces structural and visibility constraints, 3D Gaussians capture the visual realization synthesized by emitted observations. To balance stable incremental fusion with consistent readout, Paintress separates writing from reading: newly emitted frames update a persistent raw Gaussian map under confidence-gated selection, whereas a cloned reader copy is globally refined against the observation archive and rendered with coverage masks to condition generation. We also introduce Expedition-33, a benchmark for generated-appearance retention across 11 static scenes, five route families, and 15, 30, and 60 s target absences (165 settings per system). Excluded from the opening image, targets are synthesized during a shared prefix and scored against each system's own first visit at matched return cameras. Across ten systems (1,650 videos), Paintress achieves 0.1220 ROI-LPIPS, 0.0613 MAE, and 52.12% detail retention (vs. 0.2731, 0.1401, and 10.91% for CWM), with lower discrepancy at 60 s (0.1630) than CWM, AgentGarten, and Lyra 2.0 achieve at 15 s.

papers.title: Correlation-aware sequential sampling for multi-output polynomial chaos expansions
papers.abstract: The interaction of multiple physical processes in complex engineering systems is often characterized by several quantities of interest (QoIs) with non-negligible cross-correlations. Accurate uncertainty quantification of these responses requires repeated model evaluations, which can be computationally expensive. As an alternative, polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) provides an efficient surrogate modeling framework for reducing this computational cost owing to its natural structure for statistical analysis, while adaptive sequential sampling can further improve sampling efficiency under a limited model evaluation budget. However, adaptive sampling strategies specifically designed for multi-output PCE remain limited, and existing approaches commonly aggregate information from individual outputs without explicitly accounting for their statistical dependence. When strong correlations exist among QoIs, output-wise aggregation can give greater combined influence to response patterns shared by several outputs. To reduce the influence of such repeated representation on sample allocation, this study develops a principal component analysis-based extension of the multi-output criterion for adaptive construction of PCE. The sampling criterion combines component-wise normalization with the retention of selected principal directions, thereby adjusting the relative influence of shared response patterns while preserving distance-based exploration. The method is verified through numerical examples with different levels of output coupling and is compared with the conventional multi-output criterion and reference sampling strategies. The results demonstrate that accounting for output dependence improves the allocation of new samples among multiple response features and enhances the efficiency of multi-output PCE surrogate construction, particularly for strongly correlated QoIs.

papers.title: Learning the Boltzmann Collision Operator with Structural Constraints for Fast Kinetic Simulation
papers.abstract: The high-dimensional integration in the Boltzmann collision operator is a major computational bottleneck in deterministic kinetic simulations. We develop a structure-preserving neural operator that provides an efficient approximation of this nonlinear collision mapping. The operator maintains the gain-loss structure of the original Boltzmann collision operator, and, by construction, is proportional to the square of the gas density. Conservative moment projection and entropy correction enforce conservation of mass, momentum, and energy, as well as entropy dissipation. By construction, the collision term also vanishes at all Maxwellians. In the numerical scheme for simulations of gas dynamics, we establish nonnegativity of the distribution function with the learned collision operator and prove exponential relaxation to the moment-matched equilibrium when a positive spectral gap is imposed. Numerical experiments for a constant collision kernel demonstrate a favorable accuracy-cost tradeoff relative to Fourier spectral evaluations. Although trained on smooth distributions, the same operator handles discontinuous distribution functions and is embedded without retraining in steady Couette flow, normal-shock, and two-dimensional lid-driven cavity solvers. These results demonstrate a reusable approximation for repeated collision evaluations that retains kinetic structure and supports accurate deterministic simulation.

papers.title: Random Projection Neural Networks for Phase-Field Models: Model Reformulation, Scaling, and Network Architecture
papers.abstract: Phase-field models, particularly the Allen-Cahn(AC) and Cahn-Hilliard(CH) equations, are widely used to describe interfacial dynamics, but resolving their sharp transition layers and stiff dynamics presents substantial numerical challenges. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) offer a mesh-free approach, yet optimizing large numbers of network parameters can be computationally demanding and may still yield limited accuracy. We develop a random projection neural network (RPNN) framework that combines first-order PDE reformulations with independent random-feature representations of the unknowns. By fixing randomly initialized hidden-layer parameters and optimizing only the output coefficients, RPNNs reduce training to least-squares problems amenable to Newton-type solvers. Introducing auxiliary variables eliminates higher-order derivatives from the PDE residuals, while separate random feature bases in the unknowns provide flexibility in approximating fields with different scales and regularity. For the CH equation, we scale the chemical potential to address the disparity between its magnitude and that of the phase field. We compare the first-order and corresponding higher-order formulations and systematically examine the effects of initialization distributions, the random feature range $R_ξ$, seven activation functions, and dense versus separable space-time bases. We also evaluate gradient-based adaptive sampling, residual reweighting, and mild spatial derivative-penalty regularization. Across the reported benchmarks, the proposed framework reduces relative $L^2$ and absolute $L^\infty$ errors by nearly one to three orders of magnitude compared with the various PINN baselines. These results demonstrate the potential of first-order RPNNs for accurate approximation of phase-field dynamics with sharp transition layers.

papers.title: Learning How a Body Moves: Few-Shot Body Inference for Visual World Models of Animated Characters
papers.abstract: Two visually identical animated characters can respond differently to the same action command because their body dynamics differ. For example, a stiff blob and its bouncy twin reach different heights when both receive the jump command. Given only the first frame and the action command, a visual world model has no information to distinguish these twins, because their initial appearances are identical. We therefore propose an in-context world model that encodes clips of a character's other actions into a body representation, using a contrastive loss to separate look-alike characters. We introduce ToonTwins, a benchmark of 144 2D cartoon characters that run, jump, fall, turn and crouch. Its characters form look-alike groups of four that differ only in their dynamics profile, and we also evaluate the model on 32 animated animals from DeformingThings4D. Even with a body code from these clips, the latent pixel world model we tested recovered at most 25 percent of the twins' jump height difference. On new shapes, our model identified the correct twin in 85.9 percent of cases, compared with 76.7 percent for a transformer baseline that reads the same clips without a body summary, and in a controlled ablation the contrastive loss gave more than half of this gain. On the animated animals, it reduced the mean path prediction error by 8.5 percent against a model without body information.

Our main approach shares a visual encoder between tactile-image histories and RGB inputs to jointly generate and execute motion and bilateral force targets in a unified action space. Mixed real and simulated demonstrations first establish motion and contact priors. Two-stage multi-task RL then uses only simulated interaction to optimize the policy through task-success returns without continued real-demonstration supervision, and the trained policy deploys directly to real robots. We compare tactile representations and RL post-training routes in simulation and separately evaluate load variation and placement perturbations on hardware. The full method achieves higher grasping success than the supervised initialization, while RL post-training gains differ across approaches, providing empirical evidence for choosing representations and training approaches for this task.

Highaltitude navigation requires fine-grained target details and scene context relevant to visibility, but repeatedly predicting dense visual representations of this information is computationally expensive. AERIN addresses this challenge with a compact, fixedsize, target-conditioned latent state that separately represents both for efficient action evaluation. Experiments demonstrate that AERIN outperforms the evaluated baselines in target approach and observation quality, while requiring substantially less decision time than similar world models.

papers.title: RecallWorld: Episodic Memory for Persistent Embodied Video World Models
papers.abstract: Video world models generate plausible novel views but often lack persistent memory, failing to preserve a place's geometry and appearance when an agent revisits a scene. A central challenge is how previous views should be effectively used for creating memory. Reconstructing them independently underutilizes geometric constraints between nearby views, while repeatedly reconstructing a growing history can propagate later prediction errors into earlier geometry. We introduce RecallWorld, a persistent embodied video world model that jointly reconstructs short multi-view episodes into Scenelets while keeping geometry independent across episodes. Starting from a single source image, camera-aware ray lifting places perspective and native fisheye images in a common world frame, retaining wide-field content for perspective generation. Each generated segment extends the Scenelet memory and conditions subsequent generation. Coverage-based retrieval selects complementary Scenelets from the full history, while target-view visibility is resolved geometrically before appearance fusion, providing consistent memory conditioning for guiding subsequent generation. Across four datasets, RecallWorld improves revisit PSNR over the strongest evaluated baseline by 2.6 dB on partial revisits and 3.9 dB on full cycles, demonstrating substantially stronger preservation of scene identity across exploration and return.

papers.title: Persuasion from Within: Model-Based Insider Attacks in Multi-Agent LLM Debate and Consensus
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent systems for collective decision-making, such as multi-agent debate and consensus games, in which agents exchange messages and update their answers over multiple rounds and a resolution mechanism aggregates them into a final outcome. Most multi-agent LLM frameworks assume that every participant shares the system objective. In practice, however, a malicious agent can join as a legitimate member of the group and persuade the other agents toward a hidden adversarial goal. We formalize such attacks as a sequential decision-making problem in which the insider seeks to degrade the utility of the collective outcome. We propose a model-based insider attack that learns to persuade a group of agents: the insider first learns a world model of the benign agents from offline trajectories and then uses it both to train a persuasion policy and to plan its messages. In two case studies involving a numerical consensus game and a multi-agent debate, the learned insider is the most effective and the stealthiest attack we evaluate, outperforming both prompt-based and trained LLM persuaders from prior work. The attack also transfers to other target models, larger groups, and unseen datasets, and remains effective under existing Byzantine-resilience defenses. The learned insider also enables a new defense: adversarially training benign agents on the attack data largely removes both our attack and the strongest prior persuasion attack. These results show that combining world models with reinforcement learning and planning is an effective route to both attacking and hardening language-based multi-agent systems.

papers.title: Fast World Planner: Advantage-Aware Action-Chunk Policy for Online Planning
papers.abstract: Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control is central to online planning for model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL), but its iterative refinement incurs planning latency. Reducing refinement iterations often degrades performance, motivating stronger policy guidance learned from the planner. However, existing methods typically learn from the planner through action-level alignment, which does not directly capture the complete $H$-step planner proposal. Moreover, planner imitation leaves further target improvement to online refinement. To address these limitations, we propose FaSt World PlANner (SWAN), an advantage-aware MPPI-based MBRL framework that explicitly represents and improves the complete $H$-step planner proposal to improve policy guidance for efficient online planning. For proposal representation, SWAN combines k-MPPI, a multimodal MPPI extension, with a mixture of factor analyzers (MFA) action-chunk policy to capture multiple modes and correlations across time and action dimensions. For proposal optimization, we introduce Advantage-Guided Proposal Optimization (APO), which reuses MPPI evaluations to construct an improved target using advantage estimates and trains the policy toward this target while preserving planner alignment. Experiments across 31 high-dimensional continuous-control tasks from DMControl, HumanoidBench, and MyoSuite show that SWAN substantially improves control performance and sample efficiency while using 50% fewer MPPI refinement iterations than state-of-the-art planning-based MBRL methods. Finally, SWAN demonstrates zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on a physical Unitree Go2, achieving stable velocity-tracking locomotion with high-frequency control. (see our demo at https://swanfastworldplanner.github.io/)

papers.title: WorldWeave: Rethinking Embodied Navigation through Cross-Task World Modeling
papers.abstract: Mobile embodied agents continuously alter their observations through their own motion, while external dynamics further shape future interactions. Different mobile embodied tasks therefore capture complementary patterns of state evolution, yet jointly learning world dynamics across such interactions remains less explored. We investigate this problem through Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) and Embodied Visual Tracking (EVT), which respectively involve navigation toward a stationary goal and interaction with a moving target. We propose WorldWeave, a cross-task world model that couples shared predictive dynamics with task-specific adaptation. Instead of conditioning state transitions on heterogeneous physical actions, WorldWeave learns latent actions from observed state changes via inverse-forward dynamics, establishing a shared transition representation across tasks. The resulting future-state predictions are adaptively integrated into task-specific representations for downstream decision making. Experiments across multiple VLN and EVT benchmarks demonstrate consistent improvements over specialized baselines.

papers.title: PhysPPF: Learning Robotic Manipulation with Past, Present, and Future Physical Representations
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have advanced robotic manipulation, yet complex tasks requiring both precise 3D contact and long-horizon coordination remain challenging. Most existing studies enhance spatial perception or temporal reasoning in VLAs separately. Spatial methods primarily inject geometric or affordance priors into current-frame perception without tracking multi-step transitions, while history-aware and world-model VLAs typically capture past context or future dynamics in 2D feature or pixel spaces, either lacking explicit 3D contact cues or incurring high generation overhead. To address this, we propose PhysPPF, a VLA framework that performs unified spatiotemporal modeling in a compact physical token space. Spatially, WWH (What-Where-How) distills pretrained perception teachers exclusively during training into compact token groups capturing what 3D structures occupy the scene, where to interact, and how the gripper should approach, without test-time 3D encoders. Temporally, operating directly in this WWH space without pixel reconstruction, PPF (Past-Present-Future) consolidates executed states into a bounded past physical memory and jointly infers present and future physical tokens via an asymmetric world model. Parallel gated branches then inject these past, present, and future representations into a flow-matching action expert to guide manipulation without cross-temporal interference. Extensive experiments on SimplerEnv, CALVIN, and LIBERO show that PhysPPF consistently outperforms existing spatial, history-aware, and world-model VLAs with modest latency and parameter overhead, improving over the StarVLA baseline by +17.2 points on SimplerEnv, +29.3 points on CALVIN, and +3.5 points on LIBERO.

papers.title: Lifted Multiple Shooting for Parallel-in-Time Contact-Rich Trajectory Optimization
papers.abstract: Planning through contact requires accounting for the coupled dynamics of a robot and its environment, including inertial effects, contact forces, and friction. However, the non-smoothness and multimodality of contact dynamics and contact geometry makes gradient-based optimization challenging. In this work, we propose lifted multiple shooting, a trajectory optimization transcription that can be solved directly using nonlinear program solvers. By introducing contact impulses as optimization variables, our formulation allows the optimizer to satisfy the state-transition constraints using friction-cone-feasible impulses while separately enforcing their consistency with the contact model. Our formulation supports a broad class of contact constitutive relations, with sensitivities computed through implicit differentiation. To enable efficient planning over long horizons and for high-dimensional systems, we further introduce IP-PAS, a parallel-in-time primal-dual interior-point solver that achieves O(log T) parallel computational depth. We evaluate the proposed methods on six fully dynamic contact-rich planning tasks, including nonprehensile pushing and in-hand manipulation, without contact-guiding costs. Lifted multiple shooting improves success rates by up to 81.5 percentage points over standard multiple shooting, while IP-PAS achieves solution quality comparable to serial methods with up to a 3.1x speedup and scales to horizons of 40,000 timesteps.

papers.title: AlpaSafe: Risk-Aware Trajectory Selection for Vision-Language-Action Models in Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Reasoning-based driving vision-language-action (VLA) models propose multiple candidate trajectories at each decision, yet only one is executed. Standard evaluation scores the best candidate, assuming an oracle selector that deployment lacks, and leaves the risk of the executed candidate unexamined. Existing online evaluators typically close this gap with a purpose-trained scene or world model, often rolling out each candidate through it at inference time. We introduce AlpaSafe, a risk-aware trajectory selector that reuses the scene representation a frozen driving VLA computes while proposing its candidates. AlpaSafe reads the last hidden token of the VLA's prompt prefill. A lightweight head, trained on the closed-loop simulation outcomes of the candidates, fuses this token with each candidate trajectory and predicts a relative score and collision/offroad logits. A fixed rule removes candidates dominated on the two risk logits and selects the highest-scoring candidate among those remaining, adding neither rollouts nor VLA training. Experiments on 525 AlpaSim scenes show that AlpaSafe outperforms Alpamayo's default first-sample rule and uniform random selection in selected regret and top-1 agreement, and reduces the collision-at-fault or offroad rate from 6.41% and 6.10% to 4.93%. The selector has 1.7M parameters and takes 0.75 ms per decision.

papers.title: State of Mind: Learning and Evaluating World Models of Naturalistic Brain Dynamics
papers.abstract: Understanding naturalistic brain activity requires going beyond the stimulus alone, as external inputs continuously interact with an individual's evolving brain state. A world model captures such dynamics in a latent state by inferring it from neural observations, predicting stimulus-driven evolution, and updating with new observations. However, existing brain world models fail to maintain a persistent latent state over time, and standard metrics of neural prediction accuracy cannot tell whether a model tracks an individual's brain state or relies solely on the stimulus. To directly test state inference, prediction, and updating, we introduce BrainStateBench, which evaluates a model's latent state through a frozen linear probe on whole-cortex, movie-driven fMRI. Its State task tests whether a model captures trial-to-trial variability in an individual's responses to repeated stimuli, while Forecast and Updating evaluate future activity predictions without and with new observations, respectively. To track individual brain state across time, we propose Spectator, a linear latent world model trained with a joint-embedding predictive objective. Spectator encodes short- and long-horizon observation histories into a two-timescale latent state and predicts state transitions linearly from the current state and stimulus. Stimulus-only encoders reach 0.320 in fMRI prediction correlation without observing the brain (0% on State), while prior deep brain world models reach 0.239 yet score at most 0.4% on State. In contrast, Spectator achieves 0.349 correlation alongside 5.5% on State, 16.0% on Forecast, and 20.3% on Updating, outperforming all baselines while forecasting over 20x faster than deep forecasting models.

papers.title: Digital Knockoffs
papers.abstract: Social simulations often use language model agents to represent people who differ on several measurable traits. However, describing a trait profile in a prompt does not guarantee the agent will express each trait at its intended level. We propose a method that calibrates agents to multidimensional profiles using activation steering: (i) extract steering directions for each trait, (ii) learn a shared mapping from steering strengths to measured trait scores, and (iii) search for a steering intervention for each target. We use Bayesian optimization for this search and evaluate the method on the Big Five personality scores of 500 OpenPsychometrics respondents. In each of five rounds, the assigned interventions yield lower mean absolute error across respondents than the prompting and steering baselines. Further, the model's responses to a given intervention yield the same trait profile regardless of whose target motivated it, so a poor match for one respondent can be the best match for another. When we match each respondent to the closest profile found across all tested interventions, Bayesian optimization yields 16.6% lower mean absolute error than uniform random search at the same evaluation budget. Our method thus offers a way to build social agents whose measured traits dovetail with those of the people they seek to represent. Whether this closer fit translates to improved predictions of downstream behavior remains an open question.

papers.title: HiPPO Functional Memory: Coordinate-Queryable Attention for Irregular Time Series
papers.abstract: Irregular time series are recorded at nonuniform times and are often queried at other times: between observations, after the last one, or on a regular grid. Continuous-time models answer such queries by integrating latent dynamics, and time-aware attention models answer them by revisiting the observation tokens. We introduce HiPPO Functional Memory (HiPPO-FM), an attention operator that writes an irregular history into a rank-M function space with explicit time coordinates. Masked self-attention first exchanges content among the observations; the updated values are then contracted against kernel-smoothed HiPPO-Legendre features and solved through a regularized Gram matrix, so the retained coefficients define a function that is read at any time through the same features. The write and read have the form of an interdomain sparse Gaussian-process mean: every readout lies in an M-dimensional reproducing-kernel subspace, and a pointwise bound separates the approximation error of this subspace from the error of the learned memory. Removing the functional memory from the encoder raises Spiral reconstruction RMSE 18-fold. The full model has the lowest error in 11 of 12 Spiral settings, the highest overall accuracy and best average rank on 20 irregular UEA datasets, the highest event-type accuracy on all five multi-type event benchmarks, and a 21% lower extrapolation MSE than CRU on PhysioNet. Because the memory has fixed rank, the state retained after encoding keeps a fixed size as the history grows and is 102 times smaller than a token cache at 1,024 observations.

papers.title: LoKiTO: Local Kinodynamic Trajectory Optimization for UAVs based on Memory-Efficient Neural Distance Fields
papers.abstract: This paper introduces LoKiTO, a 3D local kinodynamic trajectory optimizer that combines a Chebyshev polynomial parameterization with an online neural Euclidean Signed Distance Field (ESDF) representation for aerial robotics. While current gradient-based planners often struggle with the high memory requirements of explicit volumetric maps or fail to strictly enforce dynamic limits, LoKiTO embeds kinodynamic constraints directly into a modular cost function and exploits the numerical conditioning properties of the Chebyshev basis. Collision awareness is provided by a continuous, memory-efficient neural ESDF updated online from LiDAR measurements, which drastically reduces map memory consumption to approximately 1.0 MB. Benchmarking in highly cluttered simulated environments against state-of-the-art baselines (Fast-Planner and EGO-Planner) demonstrates the superiority of our approach. Experimental results show that LoKiTO achieves over 99.4% dynamic feasibility compliance, significantly outperforming the baselines, and maintaining higher median clearance from obstacles. By coupling a well-conditioned continuous parameterization with explicit kinodynamic reasoning, LoKiTO provides a practical and extensible basis for local replanning in aerial robotics.
