papers.title: Biofunctional Dacron-Coated Porous Titanium Implants Promote Osteogenic and Soft-Tissue Integration Through Controlled Extracellular Matrix Remodeling
papers.abstract: Porous titanium implants provide excellent mechanical stability and support bone ingrowth; however, their limited intrinsic bioactivity can hinder rapid osseointegration and stable peri-implant soft-tissue sealing. This study investigates the cytocompatibility and biological responses of porous titanium implants coated with Dacron using the ethanol-induced Dacron deposition (EIDD) process, a newly developed approach, to establish a multifunctional surface interface with potential relevance to osteogenic and soft-tissue integration. Uncoated and Dacron-coated implants were evaluated using HaCaT keratinocytes, primary human keratinocytes, fetal mesenchymal stem cells, primary dermal fibroblasts, MG-63 osteoblast-like cells, and MC3T3-E1 preosteoblasts. Cell viability was assessed by MTT assay, and real-time quantitative PCR was performed to characterize gene expression associated with focal adhesion formation, integrin signaling, extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, and osteogenic differentiation. Dacron coating maintained high cytocompatibility, with cell viability exceeding 80% after 14 days across all tested cell populations. The coating was associated with increased expression of genes encoding focal adhesion-associated proteins, including focal adhesion kinase, vinculin, and paxillin, as well as integrins involved in cell–matrix interactions. Increased expression of fibronectin, vitronectin, collagen I, and matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) indicated transcriptional responses potentially associated with ECM organization and remodeling. Cell-type-specific responses included elevated MMP-2, MMP-13, and MMP-14 expression in osteogenic cells and increased MMP-1, MMP-3, MMP-9, and MMP-14 expression in fibroblasts and keratinocytes, accompanied by preserved TIMP-1 and TIMP-2 expression. In conclusion, these findings demonstrate that Dacron coating maintains cytocompatibility and modulates gene-expression profiles associated with cell–matrix interactions, ECM remodeling, and osteogenic differentiation. These transcriptional changes suggest potential relevance to bone and soft-tissue integration, although the corresponding functional effects require further direct evaluation. The results support further investigation of EIDD-mediated Dacron coating as a surface-modification strategy for orthopedic implant applications.

papers.abstract: Background: Total hip arthroplasty (THA) and bipolar hip hemiarthroplasty (BHA) are the standard procedure for severe hip pathology. Asians have different pelvic anatomy and lifestyles may result in differences of surgical outcomes. Objectives: The purpose of this study was to compare postoperative rate of dislocation within 1 year between total hip arthroplasty and bipolar hemiarthroplasty in elderly patients. Methods: This retrospective cohort study design was conducted in elderly patients with independence mobility undergone hip arthroplasty at Nakornping Hospital, Chiang Mai between July 2017 and February 2021. Rate of dislocation, revision surgery and other postoperative outcomes within one year of THA and BHA were retrieved from medical records. Results: A total of 227 patients were included, 64 THAs (28.2%) and 163 BHAs (71.8%). Five cases of THAs (7.8%) and 2 cases of BHAs (1.2%) resulted in dislocation. Three cases of THAs (4.7%) and 3 cases of BHAs (1.8%) resulted in revision surgery. THA had a higher rate of dislocation, Adjusted HR 6.36 (95% CI, 1.26-31.98), and higher risk for other outcomes including intraoperative blood loss (> 500ml), Adjusted RR 3.84 (95% CI 2.04-7.22) and operative time (> 90 min) Adjusted RR 2.16 (95% CI 1.73-2.68). Conclusion: THA was associated with a significant higher rate of dislocation, intraoperative blood loss, and longer operative time compared to BHA. BHA may be a preferable option for elderly patients requiring hip arthroplasty. However, more sample size is warranted to confirm our findings and patients related outcomes should be investigated.

papers.title: Investigating the Influence of Temperature on the Tensile Behaviour and Microstructural Features of LPBF Ti6Al4V(ELI)
papers.abstract: Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF)-manufactured Ti6Al4V(ELI) components are increasingly used in high-temperature structural applications due to their distinguished characteristics such as light weight, high strength, and biocompatibility. However, high temperatures impact their mechanical properties and ultimately reduce their service life. This study investigates the influence of elevated temperatures ranging from room temperature 20 °C to 175 °C, 325 °C, and 475 °C on the quasi-static tensile behaviour and microstructural features of high-temperature-annealed LPBF Ti6Al4V(ELI) specimens. Tensile tests were conducted under controlled thermal conditions to evaluate variations in yield strength, ultimate tensile strength (UTS), modulus of elasticity, and elongation at fracture. The results demonstrate that elevated temperatures, specifically, increasing the test temperature to 475 °C, resulted in a 36% reduction in ultimate tensile strength and a corresponding 9.7% increase in elongation compared to room-temperature conditions. These findings establish critical mechanical performance boundaries for high-temperature service applications of additively manufactured Ti6Al4V(ELI).

papers.title: Path Tracking Control of a Rice Transplanter in Paddy Fields Using Online Steering-Delay Estimation and Model Predictive Control
papers.abstract: Steering-response delays can degrade path-tracking accuracy during autonomous rice transplanting in paddy fields. This study developed a model predictive control (MPC) framework integrating online least-squares alignment time-delay estimation (LSA-TDE). The estimator aligns commanded and measured front-wheel angles to obtain an effective time shift, which updates the nominal actuator time constant through a low-frequency approximation while the transport delay remains fixed. The MPC objective includes a quadratic penalty on steering-command increments to discourage abrupt commands. Evaluation included standalone estimation tests, closed-loop simulations and 27 straight-line field runs at 1 m/s with a 20 Hz control rate. Under a prescribed time-varying shift and noise bursts, the correlation-screened estimator variant achieved a root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.0174 ± 0.0032 s (mean ± standard deviation) across 30 paired noise realisations, reducing mean RMSE by 46.21% relative to normalised cross-correlation. Field trials covered nominal initial lateral-offset magnitudes of 0.25, 0.50, and 1.00 m. The proposed controller achieved sustained line acquisition in 9/9 runs, compared with 8/9 for standard MPC without explicit delay compensation and 5/9 for Pure Pursuit. Its group-average lateral root-mean-square deviations ranged from 0.91 to 1.59 cm in common evaluation windows, representing reductions of 36.7–72.1% relative to standard MPC. These results support improved acquisition consistency and lateral tracking accuracy of the integrated framework under the tested straight-line conditions.

papers.title: Integration of Neural Network–Based Kinematic Control and Predictive Actuator Control for Robust Navigation of Differential–Driven Robots
papers.abstract: Wheeled mobile robots (WMRs) in general, and differential–drive mobile robots (DDMRs) in particular, often face challenges when navigating along a prescribed trajectory. These difficulties arise from non–holonomic constraints, nonlinear dynamics, external disturbances, and parametric uncertainties. This paper investigates a hybrid control system that combines an upper–level neural network–based controller for trajectory tracking with a lower–level actuator drive system. The drive system is based on a mathematical motor model utilizing predictive current control (PCC) methods, while simultaneously incorporating proportional–integral (PI) speed regulation. The proposed approach demonstrates superior performance, offering improved dynamic characteristics and stable kinematic behavior. Furthermore, the system exhibits high tracking accuracy, rapid convergence, and robustness against external disturbances. The proposed control system integrates an ANN–assisted PID controller for outer–loop kinematic control with an inner PI speed controller and predictive current control (PCC), based on finite–control–set model predictive control. Simulation results for circular and figure–eight trajectories, under a 100% step increase in load torque, demonstrate that the proposed approach improves tracking accuracy, shortens the initial convergence time, and reduces motor current ripple compared with the conventional PI–based control system. The study evaluates the proposed architecture through MATLAB/Simulink (version R2022b) simulations incorporating robot, actuator, converter models and voltage estimation to achieve control solutions. The results provide a basis for subsequent experimental evaluation; real–time operation and performance on a physical robot remain to be validated.

papers.title: Data-Driven Fault-Tolerant Model Predictive Control for Soft Electro-Hydraulic Actuators Using Koopman Operator and Chebyshev Neural-Network Compensation
papers.abstract: Soft electro-hydraulic actuators (SEHAs) combine compliant deformation, fast response and high force density, therefore making them attractive for soft robotics and human–machine interaction. Their electro-hydro-solid multi-physics coupling, however, produces strong hysteresis, severe nonlinearity and unmodeled dynamics, so that accurate modeling and reliable fault-tolerant control remain difficult once the actuator degrades and the measurements drift. Purely first-principle models of SEHAs rely on restrictive geometric and material assumptions, whereas black-box data-driven models are poorly interpretable and hard to embed in constrained predictive control. Finite-dimensional Koopman predictors retain interpretability but leave an approximation residual that is amplified by partial actuator failure and measurement drift; existing Koopman-based controllers neither compensate this residual explicitly nor provide fault-tolerance guarantees, and most of them are validated only in simulation. This paper develops a residual-corrected, provably bounded data-driven framework. (i) A Chebyshev-network compensator guided by a terminal sliding-mode surface (CNCTSMS) estimates the Koopman approximation residual and the lumped disturbance online, without any first-principle equation. (ii) A Koopman actor–critic model predictive control (KACMPC) is constructed, in which the critic evaluates the long-horizon value gradient and the actor emits a bounded supplementary input, so that partial actuator failure and measurement drift are tolerated without a fault-detection and isolation (FDI) module. (iii) A composite Lyapunov argument, which explicitly accounts for input saturation, actuator effectiveness loss and bounded measurement disturbances, establishes uniform ultimate boundedness(UUB) and ϵ-approximate optimality of the resulting policy. On a joint-type SEHA, the compensator lowers the identification RMSE from 2.00×10−1 to 3.61×10−3 in simulation and from 2.80×10−3 to 5.70×10−5 at 3 kV in experiment. In simulation, KACMPC reduces the tracking RMSE by 25.1% with respect to Koopman MPC under nominal conditions and by 84.0% under persistent measurement drift, as well as keeping the lowest error at every noise level tested; over 15 repeated runs, the spread of the RMSE is below 4%. In hardware experiments, only the actuator model and the one-step prediction are validated, at 2 kV and 3 kV; closed-loop fault-tolerant tracking on the physical prototype is not yet demonstrated and is stated explicitly as future work. With Np=20, the average and worst-case optimizer execution times are 3.76 ms and 5.10 ms, which fit a 10 ms (100 Hz) control period.

papers.title: Integrating Graph Neural Networks into Value-Added Models for Accountable Behavioral Health Services: A Methodological Scoping Review and Conceptual Framework
papers.abstract: Behavioral health systems increasingly use outcome data to hold programs and clinicians accountable, yet the value-added models (VAMs) used for provider profiling rely on a few administrative case-mix covariates and treat clients as independent units. This conceptual, non-empirical scoping review examined how graph neural networks (GNNs), which learn from relational big data, could serve as an auxiliary to VAM-based inference. Following Arksey and O’Malley’s framework and the PRISMA-ScR guideline, we searched Web of Science and PubMed for methodological GNN studies (2020–2025) and Web of Science and PsycINFO for methodological VAM studies (2015–2025), and charted 43 GNN and 14 VAM studies. GNN research advanced aggregation, scalability, fairness, generalization, and explainability; VAM research concentrated on covariate selection, measurement error, endogeneity, estimation, nonlinearity, multivariate outcomes, and missing data. These two literatures developed in isolation but are complementary: GNNs could recover pre-admission, network-derived case-mix information, whereas VAMs provide shrinkage, uncertainty quantification, and attributable estimates. papers.abstract: Attaining the best performance of any proposed system is the main aim of academics, researchers, and interested companies. A thermodynamic model with variable-temperature properties is developed and validated against the literature. The NSGA-II multi-objective optimization algorithm was employed to find the optimal design that balances three conflicting objectives: maximizing thermal efficiency, minimizing CO₂ emissions, and minimizing Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) to analyse system performance. A comparative analysis showed that Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) offer no computational or accuracy advantage over a classic Runge-Kutta solver for the 1D heat exchanger ODE, and thus the latter is adopted. The PINN model achieved high accuracy with a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.1341 K. A Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis was performed to quantify uncertainty in the key performance indicators. Sensitivity analyses were also conducted to evaluate the impact of key parameters on system performance.

papers.title: DEA-Assisted TME-VSG: A Physically Constrained Power-System and Data-Envelopment Framework for Robust Virtual-Inertia and Damping Tuning
papers.abstract: The increasing penetration of converter-interfaced renewable resources has reduced the physical inertia available in AC microgrids and has made frequency, voltage, power, and DC-link dynamics more sensitive to disturbances and controller settings. This paper develops a two-stage framework in which the electrical design problem is solved first and data envelopment analysis (DEA) is used only afterward to compare electrically feasible tuning policies. In the first stage, virtual inertia J and virtual damping D are selected by a constrained transient-modal-electromechanical objective that combines a normalized transient performance index (TPI), a modal stability index (MSI), and an eigenvalue-sensitivity index (ESI) over multiple disturbance and uncertainty scenarios. Particle swarm optimization provides the primary search, while Bayesian optimization is used as a solver-independent consistency check. In the second stage, each distinct feasible controller design is treated as a decision-making unit whose undesirable inputs are TPI, MSI, and ESI and whose output is one unit of feasible controller service. The DEA layer includes input-oriented CCR and BCC models, a slacks-based measure, Andersen-Petersen super-efficiency, SBM super-efficiency, assurance-region restrictions, and cross-efficiency peer appraisal. A fully specified 10 kVA grid-connected benchmark is evaluated in reduced, nonlinear averaged, and ideal switching EMT models. Five PSO runs and Bayesian optimization select J = 0.05 and D = 6; ITAE selects the same pair, so the ablation does not establish an independent benefit of every soft objective term. Forty-five distinct admissible designs supply actual performance inputs; 25 are radially efficient, indicating limited DEA discrimination. Constant unit output makes CCR and BCC equivalent. Switching peaks satisfy the stated operating limits, but two cases fail the strict settling threshold. The combined interpretation prevents DEA efficiency from being confused with electrical stability and makes the tradeoff between transient quality, modal damping, and parameter sensitivity explicit. Conclusions are restricted to the finite benchmark and numerical model assumptions.

papers.title: Influence of Thermal and Mechanical Post-Processing on the Cavitation Erosion Resistance of LPBF Maraging Steel MS1
papers.abstract: Components exposed to flowing liquids may suffer cavitation erosion, and additively manufactured parts are no exception. This study examines the effects of age hardening, shot peening, and their combination on the cavitation erosion resistance of LPBF-produced MS1 maraging steel. Four specimen conditions, as-built, age-hardened, shot-peened, and aged + shot-peened, were tested for 24 h using an ultrasonic vibratory apparatus in accordance with ASTM G32. Cumulative mass loss, mean depth of erosion (MDE), and erosion rate were evaluated, while surface damage was examined by scanning electron microscopy. All post-processing treatments improved erosion resistance compared with the as-built condition, which reached an MDE of slightly above 14 µm after 24 h. Age hardening reduced the MDE to approximately 3 µm, whereas both shot-peened conditions remained below 2 µm. The shot-peened and aged + shot-peened specimens exhibited comparable erosion behaviour, with no clear additional benefit from aging before peening. SEM observations revealed ring-like pit patterns on age-hardened surfaces, whereas damage on shot-peened surfaces was more irregularly distributed. The results indicate that shot peening substantially improves the cavitation erosion resistance of LPBF MS1.

papers.abstract: Process-based agroecosystem models such as DNDCv.CAN are usually calibrated against a single output. This leaves open whether the fitted parameters suit the other outputs. papers.title: Probabilistic multi‑scale strength prediction of sulfate‑attacked concrete using a physics‑constrained diffusion model
papers.abstract: Sulfate attack is a major durability problem for concrete in marine and sulfate-rich environments. Multi-scale homogenization links microscale phase transformations to macroscopic Mohr–Coulomb strength parameters, but its high computational cost limits uncertainty quantification. This study develops a physics-constrained diffusion model for probabilistic strength prediction of sulfate-attacked concrete. The model learns the conditional probability distribution of cohesion and friction angle from two microscale degradation descriptors. A physics-based admissibility projection embedded in each reverse diffusion step enforces non-negative cohesion and admissible friction angle bounds, preventing the accumulation of unphysical intermediate states. The multi-scale degradation physics is embedded in the training data and learned by the conditional diffusion model. The model is trained using phase composition data from a 400-day sulfate immersion test and validated against Monte-Carlo multi-scale solutions. Results show nearly 100 % physical consistency, a significant reduction in cohesion prediction error relative to an unconstrained diffusion model, and more than two orders of magnitude faster inference than direct homogenization. By learning the full conditional distribution rather than point estimates, the model captures the nonlinear and heteroscedastic dependence of strength parameters on degradation descriptors. The framework provides an efficient tool for probabilistic strength assessment and material design of concrete in sulfate environments.

papers.abstract: This study demonstrates that multi-material laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) enables spontaneous interface engineering, producing a gradient-interlocked dual-titanium laminate that overcomes the strength–ductility trade-off. LPBF intrinsically generates an interfacial transition zone that uniquely integrates a continuous compositional gradient, an interlocked morphology, and crystallographic continuity via epitaxial prior-β grains. The resulting laminate achieves a yield strength of ∼ 900 MPa and a total elongation of 16.5 %, achieving a superior strength–ductility balance. This exceptional synergy arises from two cooperating mechanisms enabled by the engineered interface. First, the gradient-interlocked structure facilitates progressive strain transfer from the hard Ti-6242S layer to the soft Ti-55511 layer. Second, this sustained strain partitioning generates a pronounced hetero-deformation induced stress that persists throughout deformation and significantly enhances the work hardening rate. The integrity of the spontaneous interface is evidenced by crack initiation within Ti-6242S (rather than at the interface) and trans -interface propagation without delamination. Crystallographic continuity inherited from a shared prior-β “skeleton” may promotes deformation compatibility across the interface. By harnessing intrinsic process phenomena to engineer interfaces unattainable by conventional methods, this work establishes a pathway for additively manufacturing heterostructures with exceptional mechanical performance.

papers.title: Disturbance-resilient augmented LQR control for robust trajectory tracking of 6-DOF quadcopters
papers.abstract: Traditional Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) controllers are widely used for quadrotor stabilization because of their simplicity and low computational cost. However, classical LQR is primarily a regulation method and lacks integral action, which leads to persistent steady-state errors during trajectory tracking, particularly in the presence of disturbances and modeling uncertainties such as wind or parameter variations. In contrast, high-performance nonlinear controllers and Model Predictive Control (MPC) frameworks improve accuracy and robustness but require significant computational resources, creating a trade-off that limits their use on embedded UAV hardware. This work addresses this gap by introducing an augmented LQR controller that embeds the integrals of position and yaw tracking errors into the state vector, enabling zero steady-state error while preserving the computational efficiency of linear optimal control. A full 6-DOF quadcopter model is linearized around hover and extended with integral error dynamics, and the optimal feedback gains are computed through the Riccati equation. Simulation results show that the proposed controller eliminates tracking error, improves transient performance by 35% (rise time reduced from 0.81 s to 0.53 s), and enhances disturbance rejection under both sinusoidal perturbations (altitude RMSE as low as 0.095 m) and intermittent wind gusts (altitude error of 0 m). These improvements are achieved with negligible computational overhead compared to classical LQR. To further validate the controller beyond the linearized model, the same feedback gains were applied to the full nonlinear quadrotor dynamics. The nonlinear-plant simulations demonstrated zero static error for moderate three-dimensional commands, successful tracking of a large-amplitude 5/30/10 m position command and 15° yaw command when introduced through a 20 s minimum-jerk trajectory, and effective disturbance rejection with an altitude RMSE of 0.0115 m under the considered sinusoidal disturbance. Furthermore, bounded helical trajectory tracking achieved position RMSE values of 0.064 m, 0.077 m, and 0.004 m along the x , y , and z axes, respectively, with peak roll and pitch angles below 8°. An instantaneous application of the same large-amplitude command resulted in attitude divergence, highlighting the importance of feasible reference trajectories and the limitations of a hover-based linear design. The augmented LQR provides an accurate and computationally efficient control solution for autonomous quadrotor trajectory tracking within the tested operating envelope.

papers.title: Computational and Machine Learning Approaches for K2NiF4-Based Cathode Optimization
papers.abstract: K2NiF4-type Ruddlesden–Popper nickelates are promising oxygen electrodes for intermediate-temperature solid oxide fuel cells because their layered frameworks accommodate non-stoichiometric oxygen and support coupled ionic and electronic transport. Their performance nevertheless depends on a complex balance among oxygen interstitial formation, defect association, migration kinetics, surface exchange, chemical compatibility and long-term stability. This review critically examines how density functional theory, correlated-electron treatments, atomistic dynamics, statistical sampling and machine learning can address these coupled phenomena in La2NiO4+δ, Pr2NiO4+δ, Nd2NiO4+δ and substituted derivatives. The methods are compared according to the properties they resolve, their underlying assumptions and their ability to reproduce experimentally relevant conditions. Particular attention is given to the distinction between experimentally established nickelate transport mechanisms and proposed data-driven optimization strategies. A defensible machine-learning workflow requires traceable composition- and condition-resolved datasets, leakage-resistant validation, uncertainty estimates and prospective experimental tests; the currently cited manuscript does not establish quantitative performance claims for several purported nickelate-specific models. Future progress depends on linking first-principles energetics, oxygen-defect thermodynamics, microstructure-sensitive electrode measurements and uncertainty-aware active learning. The resulting framework identifies testable routes toward more active, stable and reproducible K2NiF4-type cathodes.
